text: Real data always needs cleaning. Pandas has purpose-built tools for exactly the messiness you'll actually run into.

Is N-A marks which values are missing. Fill N-A replaces them with a default. Drop N-A removes the whole row instead. Which one's correct depends entirely on the business rule — a missing passenger count might mean drop the row; a missing tip might genuinely mean zero.

Drop duplicates removes exact repeats — common when combining sources, or re-processing a file twice by accident. And boolean filtering applies Lesson 16's conditions to an entire column at once. Just remember: use the ampersand and pipe symbols here, not Python's own AND and OR — those don't work correctly on DataFrames.
And sometimes a type needs fixing after the file's already loaded, not just at read time. As type converts an existing column directly, whenever you need it.

Missing values handled, duplicates gone, invalid rows filtered, types correct. Next lesson: building a simple Python ETL process — every lesson in this chapter, combined into one real script. See you there.
